_what: Trail, highlight and route links per stop, with the evidence tier for each one.
_why: The trail boxes were built when direct listing URLs could not be found, so half the named trails render as a search magnifier (135 of 265 main-loop items, 129 of 233 extension items). They can be found now. This file is the source; build_links.py injects it into STOPS/EXT_DATA. Editing the consts by hand is silently overwritten by the next build.

_tiers.official: Fetched from the managing authority (state park, NPS, USFS) and confirmed 200 with the expected content type, from this machine.
_tiers.indexed: Returned by web search with a matching title and a review count. The page itself could NOT be loaded — alltrails.com answers 403 to every request from here, so a 403 proves nothing either way. Real, but one tier below official.
_tiers.unlisted: Confirmed to exist by the managing authority, but no AllTrails listing found. Deliberately carries no trail link rather than a search that goes nowhere.

_match.exact: The official trail and the AllTrails listing are the same object.
_match.contains: The AllTrails listing is a longer user-assembled route that includes this official trail. Both are shown; the official name and length stay primary.

_uses: From the managing authority, not inferred. hike | bike | horse.
_cruise: true only where reviews support riding it at cruising pace on gravel tyres: rail-grade or packed surface, no walk sections, no puncture-hazard reports. Bike-legal is not sufficient. Technical singletrack is bike-legal nearly everywhere and is not what this flags.
_dogs: Dog rules per stop, each fetched from the managing authority and quoted. NOT generalised across authorities: the same agency gives opposite answers at neighbouring stops — Mesa Verde allows dogs on Wetherill Mesa and bans them on Chapin Mesa; Point Lobos will not let a dog stay in a parked car while Fort Ord, the other half of the same stop, has marked off-leash segments. 17 main-loop stops are deliberately still empty: the authority publishes no rule and inferring one would be the same error as a constructed URL.

For the Tombstone day trip you need no ferries and no Eagle Plains fuel stop — those matter only if the drive continues north. Still: carry at least one full-size spare, extra fuel and emergency kit, and expect no cell service, no food and no services past the highway junction. offroad.name: Salmon Glacier Road (Granduc Road)
offroad.distance: about 25 miles from Hyder at sea level to the Salmon Glacier summit viewpoint, climbing roughly 4,300 ft
offroad.difficulty: not published as a grade. Active mining road — sharp switchbacks, steep drop-offs, no guardrails, loose gravel; high clearance and durable tyres recommended
offroad.season: TIGHT AGAINST THE STOP DATES. The road is not open year-round; the usable window is roughly mid-June to September, and snowbanks can persist even mid-summer. offroad.note: The route crosses back into British Columbia above Hyder, so carry passports for the return through the Canadian border post at Stewart. Fish Creek Wildlife Observation Site is six miles up the same road, with brown and black bears on the salmon from late July into September — that part of the drive is short, paved-adjacent and worth doing even if the upper road is closed. Land-manager coverage is thin: this is a private mining road, so state tourism is the best source found and there is no BLM/USFS/BC Parks page for it.

offroad.name: Titus Canyon Road
offroad.distance: 27 miles, one way westbound, entered from Nevada Highway 374 about two miles east of the park boundary; the last 3 miles at the west end are two-way
offroad.difficulty: not graded by NPS. High-clearance two-wheel drive recommended; 4WD may be needed after storms. Rough, steep and narrow, with the canyon narrows the tightest section. Allow 2–3 hours
offroad.season: RE-VERIFY BEFORE COUNTING ON IT. NPS scheduled a full closure of Titus Canyon Road from 1 October 2026 through at least 30 April 2027 for repairs, after an earlier repair-and-reopen cycle. The stop arrives 28 Dec 2027, eight months past the earliest stated reopening — so on the face of it there is no conflict, but 'at least' is doing real work in that sentence and this road has a recent history of extended closures. Beyond that, NPS says it is often closed for snow, mud or washouts, and December storms are exactly the cause.
offroad.note: Winter is the right season for it — summer travel is not advised and the canyon floods flash. One-way means committing: once past the entrance there is no turning back for 24 miles, the road is infrequently patrolled and there is no cell service. If the through route is closed, the two-way western three miles into the narrows is still driveable in a standard-clearance vehicle and is the best part of the canyon anyway.

offroad.name: Harts Pass Road (FR 5400)
offroad.distance: climbs from Mazama in the Methow Valley to Harts Pass at 6,198 ft — the highest maintained road in Washington
offroad.difficulty: not published as an offroad grade. The Forest Service describes it as narrow and steep with only intermittent turnouts; the exposure, not the surface, is the difficulty
offroad.season: NO CONFLICT, BUT NARROW. The standing Forest Order closes FR 5400 to all motorized wheeled vehicles 1 December to 31 March every year, and snow in practice takes it from late October through to June or early July most years. The stop arrives 3 Oct 2027 — inside the open window, but within weeks of the usual first closing snow. A second, current problem: as of March 2026 Harts Pass Road is closed indefinitely from the Monument Creek Trailhead to the pass after December 2025 flood damage, with the Forest Service aiming to reopen after contractor repairs 'in early summer'. That is 2026 news, not a 2027 forecast, but it needs re-verifying before the trip.
offroad.note: Trailers of any type are prohibited on FR 5400 year-round under a Forest Order in effect since April 2014, with a narrow exemption for snowmobile trailers of 20 ft or less in two spring/autumn windows. Irrelevant here — the truck goes up alone — but it tells you what the road is like. The 3 Oct arrival is set by the larch anchor, and larch and Harts Pass are the same week, so this is the right stop for it if the road is open.

offroad.note: No listing found. No separate land-manager page exists for the spur — the Forest Service documents it only as part of the FR 5400 order, and the detailed write-ups are on hiking blogs. Recorded with no URL rather than pointing at something that is not about this road. Ask the Methow Valley Ranger District at 509-996-4003 for the gate position; the final stretch to the lookout is walk-only in some years.

scenicDrives_patch.name: S-22 Borrego–Salton Seaway (Erosion Road), with the Font's Point spur
scenicDrives_patch.note: TWO DIFFERENT ROADS, and the original entry ran them together. S-22 is the PAVED highway east out of Borrego Springs, nicknamed Erosion Road for the weathered country it crosses — a 21-mile driving tour through the Borrego Badlands with viewpoints, climbing into the Santa Rosa foothills at the east end. Font's Point is the famous overlook, and it is reached by a separate 4-MILE SANDY WASH off S-22: soft, rutted, high-clearance 4WD only, and a standard vehicle will not make it. Pavement in the coach's world, sand in the truck's.
scenicDrives_patch.season: Desert season is roughly October to April; the badlands are unusable in summer heat. Arrive 8 Jan 2028 — ideal. The wash is the hazard, not the calendar: it softens further after rain and this is flash-flood country.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: Visit California Borrego Badlands/Font's Point; DesertUSA Anza-Borrego badlands region; americansouthwest.net

offroad.name: Indian Pass Road
offroad.distance: runs north-east from Ogilby Road (County S-34) toward Picacho State Recreation Area, along the south side of the Indian Pass Wilderness
offroad.difficulty: not published as a grade. Graded desert road with sandy wash sections; the far end toward Picacho is rougher
offroad.season: NO CONFLICT — this is the right season for it. The hazard in this corner of the Colorado Desert is summer heat, not winter closure; nothing gates the road. The stop arrives 14 Jan 2028, which is prime desert-driving weather.
offroad.note: The Indian Pass Wilderness lies along the north side of the road, and vehicles are prohibited inside wilderness — stay on the designated route, which is the road itself. No BLM page exists for the road on its own; the wilderness page is the land manager's coverage of the area and is the honest link. Dispersed camping is widespread along it. Carry water and recovery gear: this is remote, sandy and effectively unpatrolled.

not_a_route.entry: Tumco (Hedges) ghost town, off Ogilby Road
not_a_route.problem: A destination, not a route. Tumco is reached by a short dirt track off Ogilby Road onto BLM Route 668, roughly 8 miles north of the I-8 exit — a few minutes of easy driving, not a 4x4 route. It should move to the points-of-interest box, where the mine history (Hedges, peak ~3,200 residents 1893–1899, renamed Tumco in 1910, abandoned 1911) and the BLM interpretive signage at the parking area are the content. Keeping it in offroad implies a drive that is not there.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Imperial Dam and Laguna Dam river road
scenicDrives_patch.note: The BLM river country north of Yuma on the California side — Imperial Dam, Senator Wash reservoir and dam, Squaw Lake, and the run down to Laguna Dam with Mittry Lake Wildlife Area between the two dams. Access from I-8 via S-24 north about 22 mi, then Senator Wash Road. There is a check-in station at Senator Wash.
scenicDrives_patch.season: LTVA permit season runs 15 SEPTEMBER to 15 APRIL — that is when this area exists as a destination and when the winter-visitor population is here. Arrive 14 Jan 2028 — peak of the season, so expect the LTVA busy. Permits: $180 long-term (the full seven months) or $40 for any 14 consecutive days.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: BLM Imperial Dam LTVA page; Visit Yuma river access map

scenicDrives_patch.name: Ogilby Road and the Cargo Muchacho mining district
scenicDrives_patch.note: Exit I-8 about 15 mi west of Yuma at Ogilby Road and run north roughly 8 mi; Tumco is signed by BLM. Gold town founded as Hedges, at least 500 people in the 1890s, abandoned 1905, renamed Tumco in 1910 after The United Mines Company. Now BLM land in the Cargo Muchacho Mountains with interpretive signage and a designated parking area. No entry fee. THE TOWNSITE IS CLOSED TO DRIVING — foot travel only past the parking area.
scenicDrives_patch.season: No gate; year-round, but this is open desert with no shade and summer is genuinely dangerous. Arrive 14 Jan 2028 — the right season for it.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: BLM Tumco Historic Mine page; Imperial Valley Press feature; mindat district records

scenicDrives_patch.name: US-95 north toward Castle Dome and Kofa
scenicDrives_patch.note: US-95 runs north from Yuma between the Yuma Desert and the Kofa refuge, which begins about 40 mi out on the east side of the highway and covers 665,000 acres. Six entrance roads lead east off the highway — Crystal Hill, Palm Canyon, King Valley, Castle Dome among them; the southernmost, about 40 mi north of Yuma, goes to the southern Castle Dome Mountains. Palm Canyon Road is at MILEPOST 85, then 7 mi of dirt east to the trailhead — Arizona's only native palms, fewer than a hundred left, plus desert bighorn. The refuge was established in 1939 for the bighorn.
scenicDrives_patch.season: No gate. Best season is the cool half of the year; the entrance roads are unmaintained dirt and washboard, and washouts after storms are the constraint. Arrive 18 Jan 2028 — ideal.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: USFWS Kofa NWR visit page; Arizona Highways; Wilderness.net Kofa Wilderness

offroad.name: Broken Arrow Trail
offroad.distance: about 3.5 miles round trip, Sedona, Red Rock Ranger District, Coconino National Forest
offroad.difficulty: sources genuinely disagree and both are recorded. The Forest Service trail page presents it as moderate with spectacular views; the off-road community rates it hard — slickrock, rock ledges and 'the Steps', with high-clearance 4WD, low range, skid plates and a short wheelbase wanted. Treat it as the harder reading and scout the Steps on foot before committing.
offroad.season: NO CONFLICT. Open year-round; spring is the best of it. The stop arrives 4 Mar 2028 — good weather, but also the start of the busy season on a route already saturated with commercial jeep tours. Go early in the day.
offroad.note: No permit is needed to drive the route, but a Red Rock Pass or an equivalent federal lands pass is required to park at the trailhead. Chicken Point, a wide slickrock overlook, is the usual turnaround and the highlight; Submarine Rock is on the way. Short enough to be a half-day from Camp Verde with the drive up.

offroad.name: Dry Creek Road (FR 152)
offroad.distance: roughly 1.1 to 1.3 miles of unpaved road from the paved lot to the upper Devil's Bridge trailhead
offroad.difficulty: not published by the Forest Service. Community reports are consistent: high-clearance 4WD required, several large rocks to clear just to get onto the road, extremely rocky and rough throughout
offroad.season: No seasonal closure found. The stop arrives 4 Mar 2028 — no conflict.
offroad.note: No listing found. Coconino NF publishes nothing specific to FR 152 that a search returned, and the detailed accounts are all on hiking blogs and paywalled offroad databases, so this is recorded with no URL rather than a link to something that is really about the hike. Its value is that it cuts the Devil's Bridge hike to about 2 miles round trip instead of the long approach — the road is a way to shorten a walk, not a destination drive. FR 152 is not recommended for pedestrians because of vehicle traffic and dust.

not_a_route.problem: A hike, not an offroad route — 32,000+ reviews on AllTrails as a trail. It belongs in the trails box. What is offroad about it is the access, Dry Creek Road / FR 152, which is now listed separately above.

offroad.name: Cathedral Valley Loop
offroad.distance: 57.6 miles, 6 to 8 hours of slow driving. Most drive it clockwise: Hartnet Road from the Fremont River ford 11.7 miles east of the visitor center, 27.8 miles to Hartnet Junction, then Cathedral Road 29.9 miles back to Highway 24
offroad.difficulty: not graded by NPS, which says high-clearance vehicles can usually manage it without four-wheel drive. That holds only when it is dry — rain or snow can make it impassable to the best high-clearance 4WD
offroad.season: THE FORD IS THE CONFLICT, NOT A GATE. The south end of Hartnet Road fords the Fremont River with no bridge; normally under a foot of water on a rocky bottom, impassable in high water, and NPS says plainly not to attempt it in flood. The stop arrives 28 Mar 2028 — spring runoff and spring storms, the worst combination for that ford, and winter snow can still leave the high sections muddy. There is no seasonal closure to check, only conditions, so this must be phoned in the day before: Capitol Reef visitor center 435-425-3791 (press #1, then #4).
offroad.note: If the ford is up, the loop is not lost — drive Cathedral Road in from the Caineville end as an out-and-back and skip the crossing entirely. That reaches the Cathedrals themselves, which is what people come for. Cell reception is poor to nonexistent on the whole loop, and there is no water; carry recovery gear and tell someone the plan. Rig advice removed from the name per the settled truck-only policy.

offroad.difficulty: BLM: "High clearance 4x4 vehicles recommended"

offroad.name: CR 240 above Angel of Shavano to North Fork Reservoir
offroad.distance: 3 mi on CR 240 from US 50 to Angel of Shavano, then 6 mi west to the reservoir
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: road "is very rough and not recommended for vehicles towing trailers. High clearance vehicles are a requirement"
offroad.season: Campground at the top operates June–September, opening and closing dependent on weather
offroad.note: North Fork is the highest-elevation campground on the Salida Ranger District at 11,000 ft, first come first served, and there is no trash service. Salida Ranger District 719-539-3591 will say how far up CR 240 has melted out.

offroad.name: Fourmile Road / Aspen Ridge
offroad.season: Forest Service: "Seasonal gates are closed December 1 and opened April 30"
offroad.note: The Fourmile Travel Management Area is 100,000 acres of joint Forest Service and BLM land; southern access is from CR 371/375, 304-308, 311, 315, 300-301 and 185. Note the two gate calendars do not match — the Browns Canyon monument roads reopen 15 Apr, the wider Fourmile gates 30 Apr — so an early-May visit is inside both windows but late April is not. The Forest Service publishes no difficulty or vehicle rating for these routes and refers visitors to the Fourmile area map or the Salida Ranger District.

offroad.name: FS Road 1434A, north boundary of Browns Canyon
offroad.season: Seasonal gate closure 1 Dec – 15 Apr
offroad.note: Worth checking before driving out there: the Friends of Browns Canyon access page states that 1434 is "an ATV trail for machines with a maximum width of 50 inches", which a full-size pickup exceeds. BLM's own page calls 1434A an ATV route without giving a width. If the 50-inch limit applies to 1434A as well as 1434, this route is not legally driveable in the truck at all — phone the Salida Ranger District (719-539-3591) rather than assume. Second source: https://brownscanyon.org/plan-your-visit/access-seasonal-closures/

offroad.name: Old Monarch Pass (FS 237)
offroad.difficulty: onX rates it 3 — Easy
offroad.season: onX lists spring, summer and fall
offroad.note: The 52.4 miles is the whole onX route, not the pass crossing — it drops off the west side, crosses Waunita Park and runs north to Pitkin, and onX warns the northern part of that descent is very rocky and rough. The pass itself is 11,375 ft, about 0.6 mi northwest of the US 50 summit, and the graded eastern side is the easy half. Recent status reports on the listing mention downed trees.

offroad.name: Turret Road (FS 184) into Browns Canyon
offroad.difficulty: BLM: "a rugged 4x4 experience into the heart of the Monument"; Friends of Browns Canyon add that "only skilled motorists looking for an extreme 4x4 experience should attempt" it
offroad.season: Seasonal gate closure 1 Dec – 15 Apr
offroad.note: Turret Road ends at a small parking area at the Browns Canyon Wilderness Study Area boundary, where it becomes Turret Trail and mechanised travel stops — so this is an out-and-back, not a through route to the river. The corridor is bighorn sheep, mule deer, lynx and Mexican spotted owl habitat, which is what the winter gate protects. Neither BLM nor the Friends group publishes a mileage. Second source: https://brownscanyon.org/turret-road/

offroad.name: Aspen Ridge
offroad.distance: not published on the free listing
offroad.difficulty: Beginner
offroad.season: Typically open 30 Apr – 1 Dec
offroad.note: Listed under its official road number, 185, and managed by the Salida Ranger District. Rated 4.4 from 47 reviews; high point 10,301 ft. Reviewers report loose rock, washout on the rock climbs and deep ruts, and that the middle section turns to mud after rain or snow — the melt-out date and the driveable date are not the same thing here.

offroad.name: Chinaman Gulch and Carnage Canyon, BLM Fourmile Travel Management Area
offroad.distance: 7.1 mi
offroad.difficulty: Difficult
offroad.season: May through October
offroad.note: FunTreks puts the round trip at about 4 hours with a high point of 8,900 ft, and names the obstacles — Rock Garden, Whale Rock, Double Whammy — most of which have bypasses on the Chinaman side. Carnage Canyon has none of that forgiveness: minimum 35-inch tires, lockers front and rear, and FunTreks tells drivers to carry and use a spill kit. It is one of the most heavily used motorised areas in Colorado, so expect company.

offroad.name: CR 306 west of Collegiate Peaks Campground toward Cottonwood Pass
offroad.season: County: "From November 1st until June 15th this road is not maintained beyond Denny Creek Trailhead"
offroad.note: The road, not the Forest Service, is Chaffee County's — Road and Bridge, 719-539-4591, is who to phone for the plough line. Their published non-maintenance window ends 15 June, later than the tag's "late May"; they aim to open the pass before Memorial Day but only as snowpack allows, and both the Chaffee and Gunnison sides gate independently. Denny Creek Trailhead is the realistic turnaround in mid-May.

offroad.name: Fourmile Area — Natural Bridge
offroad.distance: not published on the free listing
offroad.difficulty: Beginner
offroad.season: Year round
offroad.note: Rated 4.7 from 42 reviews, high point 9,218 ft. The loop runs FS 373 and part of FS 311; surface is mostly sand and smooth dirt with a few mild climbs and only small rocks, which is why it holds a year-round rating while everything above it is gated. The return leg faces the Collegiate Peaks.

offroad.name: Fourmile Travel Management Area general routes

offroad.name: Mount Antero road (FS 277), off Chalk Creek
offroad.difficulty: Difficult
offroad.season: July–September
offroad.note: FunTreks budgets 6 hours and puts the high point at 13,750 ft. The specific warning is about vehicle size rather than capability: "extremely narrow shelf road with tight switchbacks", and oversize vehicles will have a hard time at the switchbacks — a full-size pickup is the wrong shape for the top of this road even in August. Small SUVs with low range get all but the last half mile. The same road accesses Browns Lake for quiet camping.

offroad.name: Tincup Pass (FS 267) from St. Elmo
offroad.distance: 13 mi
offroad.difficulty: Difficult
offroad.season: July–October
offroad.note: About 2 hours one way, summit 12,154 ft. The blocker is specific and late: one short section of narrow shelf road at 12,000 ft holds snow into early July. Sharp rock near the top is reported to cut tires. Once clear it wants low-range gearing, skid plates and good rubber.

offroad.name: FS Road 125.B, South Mount Elbert trailhead extension
offroad.distance: 1.8 mi
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: four-wheel drive only, summer season; impassable to vehicles in winter
offroad.season: Summer only
offroad.note: The trail it serves, South Mount Elbert #1481, is 5.8 mi with 4,800 ft of gain from the lower trailhead. The road starts just beyond the lower parking lot; there is a ford about 1.5 mi up, and informal dispersed sites line the first mile if you would rather park and walk. Access is from Leadville: 15 mi south on US 24, west 3.75 mi on CO 82, then right on Lake CR 24 for 1.5 mi.

offroad.name: Hagerman Pass (FS 105), 11,925 ft
offroad.distance: 5 mi west from Leadville on Lake CR 4, then 5.5 mi on FS 105 to the summit
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: road is "very rough"; "high-clearance, four-wheel drive vehicles are recommended"
offroad.note: The Forest Service page publishes no open or close dates at all for this pass — the seasonal timing in the tag is not theirs and should be checked with the Leadville Ranger District. The 1880s railroad history is the reason the grade exists; west of the summit it continues through White River National Forest past Ruedi Reservoir to CO 82 at Basalt.

offroad.name: Hagerman Pass Road (Road 105)
offroad.distance: 5 mi west from Leadville on Lake CR 4, then 5.5 mi on FS 105 to the summit
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: road is "very rough"; "high-clearance, four-wheel drive vehicles are recommended"
offroad.note: Same road as the Hagerman Pass entry above — one route, listed twice in this box. The Forest Service publishes no seasonal dates for it.

offroad.name: Halfmoon Road (FS 110) to Elbert Creek and the Mount Massive trailhead
offroad.difficulty: not rated by the Forest Service on this page
offroad.note: The authority page confirms the road and what it reaches — FS 110 follows the southern border of the Mount Massive Wilderness and serves several campgrounds plus the Mount Massive and North Elbert trailheads — but publishes no surface, mileage or vehicle guidance. The Forest's own trail pages add that the road is not maintained in winter and that the last half mile to the trailhead needs high clearance and 4WD. Very busy in summer.

offroad.name: Mosquito Pass (FS 438)
offroad.distance: 9.5 mi
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: "moderate to difficult, steep and very rocky"
offroad.season: Forest Service: "usually only open for six to eight weeks after the snow melts in July"
offroad.note: The Forest Service signs and numbers this as County Road 12, not 438 — worth knowing at the junction. The tour starts from Fairplay: north on CO 9 for about 4.2 mi, then left onto CR 12, and the interpretive stops begin almost immediately. The brochure is a download from this page as well as a paper copy at the South Park Ranger District.

offroad.name: Mosquito Pass Road
offroad.distance: 9.5 mi
offroad.difficulty: Forest Service: "moderate to difficult, steep and very rocky"
offroad.season: Forest Service: "usually only open for six to eight weeks after the snow melts in July"
offroad.note: Same road as the Mosquito Pass (FS 438) entry above — one route, listed twice in this box. Signed as County Road 12 from the Fairplay side.

offroad.name: Boulder Lake Road (CR 125 to FS 370780)
offroad.distance: about 24 mi from Pinedale, roughly 10 mi of it dirt and gravel
offroad.note: The Forest's own directions match the tag turn for turn, and add that the dirt and gravel section is simply bumpy rather than technical — no 4WD language anywhere on the page, which is what makes this the sane shakedown day. The campground at the end has 15 sites on the east end of the lake near Boulder Creek.

offroad.name: Green River Lakes Road (FS 370650)
offroad.distance: 25 mi paved on WY 352 to the forest boundary, then 18 mi of dirt — about 50 mi from Pinedale
offroad.difficulty: "While the dirt road to the campground is suitable for 2 wheel drive vehicles, weather can make this road impassable to all but 4 wheel drive vehicles"
offroad.note: One thing to check before the trip rather than at the junction: the Bridger-Teton began a major reconstruction of this road in July 2026 — grading, drainage, culverts and new aggregate — with Phase 2 from the Union Pass Y to Green River Lakes scheduled for Aug–Oct 2026 or summer 2027. It should be finished and in better shape by 2028, but the Forest's conditions page is where any carryover work would be posted: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r04/bridger-teton/conditions/green-river-lakes-road-construction-updates . Lower Green River Lake sits at 8,000 ft; drinking water at the campground only 1 Jul – 15 Sep.

offroad.name: New Fork Lake access (FS 370730 / 370735)
offroad.distance: about 24 mi from Pinedale — 6 mi US 191, 14.4 mi WY 352, 3 mi CR 162, then under a mile on FS 370730
offroad.note: Shorter and less committing than the tag implies — the forest road portion is under a mile, with the 3 mi of county road before it. The Forest publishes no road-surface warning, no high-clearance requirement and no seasonal date for this approach; the only figures on the page are the distances above. Third-party sites describe the last stretch as rocky, but that is not the Forest's wording and is not sourced here.

offroad.name: Union Pass Road (FS 370600)
offroad.note: This is the Forest's own road-conditions page and it is the only official page that names NFSR 600 by number: Union Pass Road runs from the forest boundary to the Green River Lakes Road (NFSR 650) junction, the "Union Pass Y". Phase 1 reconstruction covered exactly that segment in July 2026 with 30-minute delays and one full closure day; work may carry into 2027, so check this page before driving it. The Forest publishes no mileage, difficulty or open date for the road — the Pinedale Ranger District (307-367-4326) and the MVUM are the authority for what is open. The 70-plus-mile Dubois-to-Pinedale figure that circulates online is not a Forest Service number and should not be relied on.

offroad.name: Robidoux Pass / Carter Canyon gravel loop
offroad.distance: 23 mi as a loop — out on Carter Canyon Road, back on Robidoux Road
offroad.note: No land-management agency publishes this route: the pass is a National Historic Landmark on private and county ground, and the reconstructed 1851 Robidoux trading post in Carter Canyon is run by the Friends of Robidoux Trading Post, not a park service. That means no road-condition page, no seasonal gate and nobody to phone about surface after rain. Access is two miles south of Gering on Hwy 71 then eight miles west. Pioneer graves and wagon ruts are visible along the route; self-guided, no facilities. The Nebraska State Historical Society publishes the history of the pass but nothing about the road, and its page would not load for verification, so it is not linked here.

offroad.name: Black Hills National Forest Forest Road 307 (FR307) area
offroad.note: No route listing exists for FR 307 — not on Trails Offroad, not on onX, and no Forest Service page names the road. It shows up only as a dispersed-camping area in third-party campsite directories. The Forest's Motor Vehicle Use Map is the only authority for whether FR 307 is open and to what, and it is the document to carry: motorised travel off a designated road is limited to 300 ft for dispersed camping, camp 100 ft from any creek and half a mile from developed sites, 14 days in any 60-day period, and open campfires are prohibited in the South Dakota portion of the forest. The MVUM itself is obtained from the Forest's maps and guides page, free from district offices or online: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r02/blackhills/maps-guides

offroad.name: Captain Crunch (Johnson Siding, near Rapid City)
offroad.distance: not published on the free listing
offroad.difficulty: 10 out of 10 — Trails Offroad calls it possibly "the most difficult, rock-crawling trail in South Dakota"
offroad.note: Filed as a scout route rather than a full trail guide, and rated 5/5 from a single review, so the listing is thin. It is in the "Cereal Bowl" area off Bogus Jim Road and starts where the Got Milk? trail starts, which means you can walk in down the smoother north section to spectate without committing the truck. Sedan-sized boulders, v-notches and steep climbs; purpose-built buggies only. Trailer parking at the Cereal Bowl entrance, no camping on the trail.

offroad.name: China Gulch Road, Black Hills NF (Hill City)
offroad.difficulty: Beginner
offroad.season: Typically open 15 May – 15 Dec
offroad.note: Official road number is 249, Mystic Ranger District; rated 4.2 from 14 reviews, high point 5,743 ft, and it is a through route rather than a loop. It starts in China Gulch and runs into the rougher Nugget Gulch area, with the creek crossings concentrated near the northern end — so the easy rating applies to most but not all of the 12.75 miles.

offroad.name: Lightning Creek Road, Black Hills NF (Custer)
offroad.distance: not published on the free listing
offroad.difficulty: Moderate
offroad.season: Year round
offroad.note: Official road number is 288, Hell Canyon Ranger District; rated 3.7 from 4 reviews, high point 6,579 ft, through route. Crazy Horse Memorial is visible from the northern section. Note the grade is Moderate, not easy as the tag suggests — the free listing gives no reason for that, so it is worth reading the full guide or asking the district before committing.

offroad.name: Moses Hill (between Sturgis and Nemo)
offroad.difficulty: not published on the free listing — Trails Offroad describes it as manageable for beginners in the right vehicle but intimidating to look at
offroad.note: Under a mile long, which makes it an add-on rather than a day. It runs off Vanocker Canyon in Lawrence County, is single-vehicle width the whole way over loose rock, and gets slick and genuinely risky in the wet. Short-wheelbase high-clearance with low range is the recommendation; long-wheelbase vehicles need extra clearance for the rock ledges and low-clearance vehicles will hang up. Rated 5/5 from 6 reviews. No camping on the trail itself; dispersed camping on the roads nearby.

offroad.name: Bell Lake Road / FH2 to the Elkhorn Ranch Unit
offroad.distance: from the South Unit: 8.8 mi gravel on CR 11, 6.5 mi Westerheim Road, 11.7 mi Bell Lake Road, then 3 mi on FH 2 to the parking area. From the North Unit it is Black Tail Road/FH 2 for 12.2 mi gravel, then Bell Lake Road for 3 mi and FH 2 for 3 mi.
offroad.difficulty: NPS: the last 3 miles "sometimes needing 4-wheel drive or high-clearance vehicles", particularly in winter or during and after rain showers
offroad.note: Two things NPS flags that matter more than the road itself: there is no cell signal anywhere on the route, and there are no visitor centres or facilities at the unit. Check conditions at a visitor centre before setting out — that is the park's own instruction, not a suggestion. From the parking area a 0.7 mi mowed path leads to the cabin site.

offroad.name: Little Missouri National Grassland section roads
offroad.distance: 1,033,271 acres — the largest national grassland in the country
offroad.note: The official acreage is 1,033,271, slightly above the 1.025 million in the tag. Two districts split it: McKenzie Ranger District in the north, Medora Ranger District in the south — Medora is the one to phone from this stop. The Forest Service publishes no surface guidance, no 2WD/4WD rating and no gumbo warning on this page, so which section roads are open and to what is a Motor Vehicle Use Map question, not something to infer from the map lattice. The 144-mile Maah Daah Hey Trail crosses the same ground, and the page lists 11 campgrounds and 11 OHV road-riding sites.

Knife River Indian Villages National His.entity: Knife River Indian Villages National Historic Site

Devil's Kettle at Judge C. R. Magney Sta.entity: Judge C. R. Magney State Park

offroad.name: Forest roads inland from the Caribou Trail (Cook County Rd 4) toward the Sawtooths
offroad.note: The Forest Service treats this ground as four linked signed routes: Beaver Dam, Moose, Maple Leaf and Mountain View Drives. The route-name signs go up only for the fall colour season, so navigation is by map the rest of the year. USFS publishes no mileage, surface or difficulty for any of the four.
offroad.season: Cook County puts spring load restrictions on gravel roads at 5 tons/axle for a minimum of eight weeks, and notes they not uncommonly run past the MnDOT North Frost Zone dates — a useful proxy for when this gravel is soft. Lifted 26 Jun in 2026.

offroad.name: Superior National Forest gravel spurs off the Gunflint Trail
offroad.distance: 57 miles Grand Marais to Trail's End Campground (the byway itself; the spurs are unmeasured)
offroad.note: The Gunflint Trail is paved — the gravel is all in the spurs off it, and USFS publishes no inventory of them. Forest Service wording for this road network generally: single lane with occasional wide turnouts, you may have to back up for oncoming traffic, and logging trucks use them. Gunflint Ranger District office runs 1 May to 30 Sep. Check the forest alerts page before committing to a day out.

offroad.name: No 4x4 routes inside the park
offroad.note: Confirmed by omission rather than by a quoted ban: the DNR park page lists the park's activities in full — snowmobiling, cross-country skiing, dog sledding, hiking, hunting, metal detecting, paddling — and ORV/ATV riding is absent. The DNR does name ORV riding explicitly at sites that have it, so the omission carries weight, but the actual prohibition text lives in the Land Use Orders of the Director Chapter V, which could not be opened. Treat as an absence of listing, not a quoted rule.

offroad.name: Ottawa National Forest roads toward Bond Falls and Agate Falls
offroad.season: Bond Falls: vehicle access typically mid-May through mid-October, weather depending; the hiking-trail access is open year-round. Ottawa NF routes designated 'Seasonal' are open 16 May through 14 Mar annually.
offroad.note: Bond Falls and Agate Falls are Michigan DNR scenic sites, not Forest Service ones, so their gate dates come from DNR and the road designations from the Ottawa. Watch the Ottawa's 65-inch OHV width rule — it excludes a full-size pickup from the designated OHV trails, but not from Forest Service roads open to highway-legal vehicles on the MVUM. Agate Falls was closed through late 2026 for trestle bridge repairs; long finished by 2028 but worth one re-check.

offroad.name: Shore-road spurs off M-64 east toward Ontonagon
offroad.note: No listing of any kind exists for these spurs — no Forest Service page, no route database, no club page. The road authority is the Ontonagon County Road Commission, which maintains every local shore spur off M-64 and is also the body the DNR names as deciding when South Boundary Road reopens each spring; its site returned 403 and is deliberately not linked here. M-64 itself is fully paved, so all the gravel is in the spurs, and no published inventory names them individually.

offroad.name: South Boundary Road, Union Bay end to Presque Isle end
offroad.season: DNR wording: park roads, including County Road M-107 at the Whitetail parking area and South Boundary Road from Headquarters Road south to the Pinkerton Trailhead, close Dec. 1 through late spring for visitor safety.
offroad.note: There is no fixed reopening date — the roads become designated snowmobile trails over winter and reopen to vehicles only when the Ontonagon County Road Commission deems them safe, so the Union Bay to Presque Isle through-drive is not guaranteed until they say so. The DNR publishes a workaround: the Presque Isle end stays reachable via County Road 519 just east of Wakefield. Park office 906-885-5275.

offroad.name: Co. Rd. AAA (Triple A Road), Yellow Dog Plains
offroad.distance: 11.9 mi, Big Bay to Yellow Dog Plains, +1,060 ft
offroad.difficulty: Moderate (the site's own scale)
offroad.note: Only the eastern half is suitable for standard vehicles — at the western edge of Yellow Dog Plains the road deteriorates into large puddles, big rocks and steep inclines that challenge even high-clearance vehicles, so plan to turn around there and run it as an out-and-back from Big Bay. There is no signage marking the turn off County Road 510; navigate by odometer. Naming trap: the same road is Co. Rd. AAA in Champion Township but Co. Rd. KAA in Powell Township, so signs and maps will disagree along its length. This source is a driving-route site, not a land manager — the turn-around advice is uncorroborated by any authority.

offroad.name: County Road 510
offroad.season: Marquette County seasonal weight restrictions historically go on mid-March and come off mid-May — in 2026, on 5 Mar and lifted 8:00 a.m. 18 May. Loads cut to 65% of normal legal load; the pickup is nowhere near the limit, but the dates mark when the dirt section is soft.
offroad.note: No route database lists this road. The Road Commission publishes an All Season Roads list by township and a status line on 906-486-4491 opt. 2.

offroad.name: Old CR-510 steel bridge over the Dead River
offroad.distance: 271.0 ft structure, 265.0 ft main span, 19 ft roadway width
offroad.note: The fact that changes the plan: the bridge is CLOSED to vehicles — open to traffic 1921, closed 2010 — so you cannot drive it. Marquette County left it standing for its historic value and it remains open to pedestrians, with a walkway approaching it on an even grade; signs read 'MCRC Property Enter At Own Risk'. It is the longest pin-connected highway truss span in Michigan and the type is extremely rare in the state. Reach it from the old CR 510 approaches, now County Road JWW and County Road JHH, or view it east of the new crossing. Park and walk, not a drive.

offroad.name: Chapel Road (H-58 to Chapel Basin trailhead)
offroad.distance: 5 miles north off Alger County Road H-58, about 15 miles east of Munising; 17.8 mi from Munising, 34.2 mi from Grand Marais
offroad.difficulty: "a rough, backcountry road" — NPS wording; NPS publishes no rated scale
offroad.note: Heavy congestion in summer and early fall, and the trailhead lot often fills by 9 am — an early start matters more than the road does. Seasonal vault toilet, no drinking water. NPS publishes no winter gate date for this road; the park's conditions page carries only weather and ski grooming and has no road section at all.

offroad.name: H-58 spurs to Miners Beach, Little Beaver Lake and Hurricane River
offroad.note: NPS publishes distances to each spur but not the length of the spurs themselves: Miners Castle Road 5.2 mi from Munising, Little Beaver Lake Road 22.8, Hurricane River lower entrance 40.8 and upper 41.1. No difficulty or seasonal gate dates are published for any of them.

offroad.name: Hiawatha National Forest roads south of H-58
offroad.distance: over 2,000 miles of Forest Road open to motorized use, forest-wide
offroad.note: The MVUM classifies by permission, not difficulty — 'Roads Open to All Vehicles' versus 'Roads Open to Highway Legal Vehicles Only', and the pickup is the latter. Hard rule, verbatim: motor vehicle use off designated routes, including for game retrieval, is prohibited, with penalties up to $5,000 or 6 months regardless of the presence or absence of signs. Seasonal routes are flagged per-road on the sheet's Seasonal and Special Designation Table, not by one forest-wide date. MVUMs are reissued annually — pull a fresh one before the trip.

offroad.name: Crisp Point Light access roads (Luce County / forest roads west of Whitefish Point)
offroad.distance: CR 412 Crisp Point Rd, CR 423 to Singleton's Driveway and CR 502 to Crisp Point — 11.60 miles; approach CR 414 Pike Lake Rd, CR 407 to just west of Pike Lake — 11.27 miles
offroad.season: Luce County Road Commission seasonal roads list, Rev. 03/07/2023: not maintained for public travel from November 1 to April 30. The lighthouse society adds that the last 7 miles of CR 412 are usually open by the end of May, and that snow can make the road impassable even in spring.
offroad.note: This is the road authority's own seasonal-roads list, so it is the harder source than the lighthouse society's directions page the sibling entry links. Worth knowing the winter status: the road becomes Snowmobile Trail 8, and the society's own warning is not to drive it when there is snow. Watch for ATVs on the dirt.

offroad.name: Lake Superior State Forest two-tracks toward the Two-Hearted River mouth
offroad.distance: CR 423, CR 414 to the Mouth of the Two Hearted — 4.34 miles (Luce County Road Commission)
offroad.season: The county-road spine in is not maintained for public travel November 1 to April 30.
offroad.note: Honest limit: the graded county roads that get you in are fully documented, but no authority page describes the individual named two-tracks off them — treat the spine as listed and the two-tracks themselves as unlisted. This Newberry-approach directions page is the distinct source (the sibling entry carries the Paradise approach): roughly 37 miles, about 1 hour 10 minutes, and once off M-123 the roads are all dirt or sand, narrow and curvy. The society's own line is that they cannot guarantee you won't get stuck.

offroad.name: Vermilion Road toward the old Coast Guard station
offroad.distance: roughly 13 miles: from Paradise north on N. Whitefish Rd 5.2 mi, left on Vermilion Rd, 0.6 mi keeping right, then 6.1 mi on the straightest road, then 1.3 mi to the preserve
offroad.note: This is not a drive-through. Motorized vehicles, including ATVs and snowmobiles, are prohibited on the Vermilion Point preserve itself, so you drive the road to the boundary and walk to the old life-saving station — if the card implies driving to the station, that is wrong. Dogs are NOT allowed at the preserve 1 May to 15 August; leashed only the rest of the year. 175 acres, 9,240 ft of Lake Superior frontage, station first built 1876. Vermilion Road is in Chippewa County and is absent from the Luce County seasonal list; whether it carries its own seasonal designation is unknown.

offroad.name: Emmet County shore roads west of Mackinaw City toward Cross Village
offroad.difficulty: Road Commission's own wording: seasonal roads "are not typical road beds and are often narrow, swampy, and can often be difficult to navigate"
offroad.season: A seasonal road will not be maintained November through April, and will not be open to public traffic during that time — though the Road Commission states plainly that it does not enforce any closure. Grading happens once or twice a year, typically late spring through early fall. No winter plowing.
offroad.note: No listing exists for this as a named 4x4 route; this is the road authority confirming the roads and how they are managed. Live caution as of mid-2026: four separate M-119 segments were closed after April 2026 flooding, plus Lower Shore Dr — the corridor was still under FEMA disaster recovery. Check MDOT's MiDrive before relying on the through-route.

offroad.name: Wilderness State Park two-tracks (Sturgeon Bay / Waugoshance Point)
offroad.season: The plover closure is in state law, not just park signage: Land Use Orders of the Director 5.7(1)(b) closes the posted lands April 15 through August 31, and 5.7(1)(c) separately bars possessing or allowing a dog on them at Waugoshance Point and Sturgeon Bay over the same April 15 to August 31 window. The park page adds that the shoreline outside pet-friendly areas is closed to pets April through August.
offroad.note: DNR names Nebo Trail, South Boundary Trail, Swamp Line Trail and Sturgeon Bay Trail as two-tracks, and notes many visitors ride Waugoshance Point Road. Park is 11 miles west of Mackinaw City, 26 miles of Lake Michigan shoreline. The dog is the binding constraint here, not the truck — check the arrival date against April 15 to August 31 before planning this one. Recreation Passport required for vehicle entry.

trails.stats_note: Our card name pairs two things NPS treats differently. NPS lists no 'Dune Climb' as a standalone trail — it is a trailhead, and the trail leaving it is the Dunes Hiking Trail (3.5 mi, Strenuous), which is NOT the Cottonwood Trail. The 1.5 mi / Moderate figures are the Cottonwood Trail alone. Worth splitting this into two entries, or renaming to 'Cottonwood Trail'.

other_links.label: Wisconsin DNR — Peninsula State Park hiking
other_links.note: Managing authority. A 0.6-mile portion is graveled for universal access — the flattest option on this stop.

other_links.label: Wisconsin DNR — Peninsula State Park hiking
other_links.note: Managing authority. Runs below 150-foot cliffs past springs and forested terraces. 'More difficult' is the DNR's own three-step scale (Easiest / Moderate / More difficult), not an AllTrails grade.

other_links.label: Indiana DNR — Indiana Dunes State Park
other_links.note: Managing authority. The route is the park's Trail 8, 1.5 miles, graded RUGGED, which 'covers the three highest dunes'. DNR lists the 3 Dune Hiking Challenge as an activity but publishes no separate spec for it.

trails.stats_note: Figures are Indiana DNR's for Trail 8, the trail the challenge follows. 'Rugged' is the DNR's own top grade (Easy / Moderate / Rugged).

other_links.label: Grand River Conservation Authority — Elora Quarry
other_links.note: Managing authority confirms the trail exists: a one-kilometre loop through cedar forest, in places overlooking the Grand River. GRCA gives it no formal proper name and publishes no difficulty grade.

trails.stats_note: GRCA describes this as 'a one kilometre loop trail', not as a named trail — our card name is a descriptive label, not the authority's.

other_links.note: Managing authority. Highway 60 km 42.5. Accessible boardwalk through black spruce bog.

trails.name: Beaver Pond Trail
trails.stats_note: Name collision worth guarding against on merge: Murphys Point Provincial Park (stop perth-on) also has a 'Beaver Pond Trail', 1 km and Easy. These figures are Algonquin's.

offroad.name: Rock Lake Road (Hwy 60 km 40.3 to Rock Lake)
offroad.distance: 8 km of gravel south from Highway 60 to the Rock Lake Campground, then 150 m to the access point on the Madawaska River
offroad.season: Rock Lake Campground open mid-May to October; Ontario Parks gave the 2026 window as May 8 to October 18.
offroad.note: The two authorities differ slightly on the turn — the Friends of Algonquin say km 40.3, Ontario Parks say km 40. Neither publishes a gate date for the road distinct from the campground season, and the Friends page defers to Algonquin Park Advisories for road conditions. Access point at 45.525077, -78.413210.

trails.distance: 2.5 km loop (plus a 1 km loop at the beginning)

other_links.label: Ontario Parks — Sandbanks activities
other_links.note: Managing authority. Confirms name, length, grade; notes a barrier-free section.

trails.name: Woodlands Trail
trails.distance: 3.5 km linear (7 km out and back)

other_links.label: Ontario Parks — Sandbanks activities
other_links.note: Managing authority. Interpretive trail; Ontario Parks publishes no difficulty grade for this one.

offroad.name: Point Petre / Ostrander Crown Land Block access roads
offroad.season: Ontario Parks states conservation reserves do not have operating dates.
offroad.note: Material change the existing note predates: this land was re-designated in 2023. Point Petre Provincial Wildlife Area and the Ostrander Point Crown Land Block are now the Monarch Point Conservation Reserve, 1,607 ha, regulated under the Provincial Parks and Conservation Reserves Act, 2006 — so any framing of it as MNRF Crown land is out of date. The regulation notice says vehicle use "will be permitted to continue on trails, or off trail to retrieve game, as long as the values the conservation reserve was created to protect are not adversely impacted," and warns that timing restrictions or trail closures could be added later. No management plan with a road inventory exists yet, so no authority publishes mileage, ratings or gate dates. Sandbanks Provincial Park (613) 393-3319 is the only way to get a current answer.

trails.name: Silver Queen Mine Trail (Murphys Point Provincial Park)

other_links.label: Ontario Parks — Murphys Point activities
other_links.note: Managing authority. Bikes permitted on the gravel roadbed portion only — the bike use is partial, not whole-trail.

trails.name: Rideau Trail (Murphys Point / Perth section)
trails.distance: 6 km inside the park (part of the ~300 km Rideau Trail)

other_links.label: Ontario Parks — Murphys Point activities
other_links.note: Managing authority for the in-park section. The wider Rideau Trail is managed by the Rideau Trail Association, not verified this session.

trails.stats_note: The 6 km and Easy grade describe only the segment inside Murphys Point. The full Rideau Trail is roughly 300 km and is not graded here.

offroad.name: Lanark Highlands gravel township roads (Perth north toward Lanark, Flower Station and Ompah)
offroad.distance: approximately 350 km of gravel roads in the township, many of them seasonal, across 1,048 km²
offroad.season: Two separate restrictions, and the second is the one that bites. Reduced loads are usually in effect from March 1st to mid-May. Seasonal Roads — Class 6B and Class 6C — are CLOSED between November 15 and April 15. That is an outright closure of the seasonal gravel, not a weight limit.
offroad.note: Manager of Public Works 613-259-2398 ext. 239; road emergency 613-264-7329.

offroad.name: Upper Works Road (CR 25A)
offroad.distance: 3.3 mi
offroad.difficulty: 1 (Easy) — onX rates it 1/10 for smooth, well-maintained gravel and dirt with no significant obstacles
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall. Neither the Town of Newcomb nor DEC publishes a winter plowing status or gate date for this road.
offroad.note: Ends at a large parking area with a pit toilet, and passes the historic McIntyre Blast Furnace of the Tahawus ghost town — you can drive to the gate, the rest of the ghost town is on foot. The road follows the Hudson close to its source, past marshes and ponds. Naming caveat worth carrying: the Town of Newcomb and DEC call the county route CR 25 (Tahawus Road), not CR 25A, and the Town states the old parking lot at the terminus of Upper Works Road is closed, with parking moved to a 60-car lot by the MacNaughton Cottage and unauthorised vehicles towed. The draw is history and trailhead access rather than the driving.

offroad.name: Deer Pond Road
offroad.distance: 2.2 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — rated 2/10, mostly easy dirt with minor potholes and muddy puddles after rain
offroad.season: DEC requires parking reservations from Memorial Day weekend until the gates close for winter in late November or early December.
offroad.note: Resolved to the Essex Chain Lakes Complex in Newcomb, where DEC calls it the Cornell/Deer Pond Road — not Moose River Plains. Ends at a large parking area on the edge of the Essex Chain Lakes Primitive Area with a pit toilet and a gate; you continue on foot to the water. Several roadside dispersed camp spots along it. DEC's own wording for the roads here: pickup trucks, SUVs and other high axle vehicles are recommended, four wheel drive will serve even better. Beavers occasionally flood portions of the road.

offroad.name: Otter Brook Road
offroad.distance: 2.9 mi, out-and-back
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — not very difficult, but one vehicle wide and needing some higher clearance toward the end
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall. DEC publishes no fixed gate dates for Otter Brook Road itself; the parent access, the Limekiln Lake–Cedar River Road, is a seasonal road that opens mid-May.
offroad.note: DEC-maintained, in the Moose River Plains Complex, and it sees very little traffic. Surface alternates sandy two-track and well-maintained gravel; it ends at a bog where a small snowmobile bridge crosses the South Branch of the Grass River. Live closure to check before going: a bridge failure at Payne Brook has forced all Moose River Plains access to the Limekiln Lake/Inlet entrance, with the Cedar River Headquarters gate closed — approach from the west. DEC Region 5 Northville 518-863-4545.

offroad.name: Lake Glen Road
offroad.distance: 6.6 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — an established forest access road with a stable base, no deep waterholes or large rocks
offroad.season: Best summer and fall; no gate dates published by anyone.
offroad.note: Runs around the southern flank of 3,550 ft Saddleback Mountain through the Adirondack Forest Preserve. Side-trail access at the western end is blocked by a forest products company that owns most of the surrounding land. Honest limit: this is the one Adirondack route no authority confirms — no DEC page, unit management plan or roads-open-to-motor-vehicle-use listing names it, and because it runs between Forest Preserve and private industrial timberland its legal access basis is genuinely unestablished. Recent reports include downed trees needing recovery boards in Dec 2025.

offroad.name: Patterson Brook Road (Fire Service 50)
offroad.distance: 5.2 mi, out-and-back
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — easy driving, but care is needed because active logging changes road conditions; a chainsaw for blowdowns helps
offroad.season: Green Mountain National Forest, official: most GMNF roads are closed during the winter months from December 15 to May 1, with some exceptions. FR 50 Patterson Brook, Rochester district, currently listed Open.
offroad.note: The one route in this set with a real land-manager behind it. Borders the Bread Loaf Wilderness, climbing from 1,043 ft near Granville to 1,868 ft. Dispersed off-grid campsites along FR 50, no permit, 14-day limit, and no cell service. Stream crossings are on good bridges.

offroad.name: Symonds Mill Road
offroad.distance: 4.1 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — "country dirt roads"
offroad.season: Best fall, summer, spring. No town or state mud-season restriction found for this road.
offroad.note: The one Vermont route in this set that is genuinely local to the stop — Wolcott/Elmore, about 20 minutes from Stowe. Mostly packed gravel with some muddy sections; these are working farm roads, so watch for farm equipment and livestock. Pairs with Woodbury Mountain Road if you want a longer day.

offroad.name: Big Hollow Road
offroad.distance: 6.2 mi
offroad.difficulty: 3 (Easy) — varied surface from packed gravel to dirt to mud
offroad.season: Best fall and summer. A status report of 14 Apr 2026 has it Temporarily Closed for a posted seasonal closure, with no stated opening day — consistent with a Vermont Class 4 mud-season closure. Best avoided during spring sugaring season.
offroad.note: Location flag worth resolving before the trip: this listing sits at 44.227, -73.056, which is Starksboro in Addison County — west of the Green Mountain spine and about 35 miles from Stowe, not the Fayston Big Hollow Road. Fayston's town roads page and its 2020 Town Plan both fetch clean with no mention of a Big Hollow Road, so no listing for the Fayston one could be sourced. Starts as farm gravel, becomes a standard Class 4 road with small obstacles, past abandoned homes and maple sugaring equipment; narrows at a log landing halfway, then an older, less-used trail out into a field with horses.

offroad.name: Top of the World
offroad.distance: 3.8 mi
offroad.difficulty: 3 (Easy) — maintained gravel that washes out on the steeper climbs, with water bars that can catch a low bumper
offroad.season: Best time listed as summer only.
offroad.note: Same location flag as Big Hollow: this runs the powerlines on the Vermont side of Moore Reservoir, near Waterford in Caledonia County — roughly 50 miles east of Stowe, a long day trip rather than a local run. No Roxbury or Northfield 'Top of the World Road' could be sourced anywhere. The payoff at the top is a view over Moore Reservoir toward New Hampshire. Many offshoots from mild to wild; the final climb is where 4WD matters if it has washed out. Expect ATV and side-by-side groups on a fine day. Reports through 2026 say a washout has been repaired and the route rebuilt into an easy dirt road.

offroad.name: Jefferson Notch Road
offroad.distance: 8.4 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — wide enough for vehicles to pass almost anywhere, though storms leave ruts and washouts
offroad.season: Gate dates, from 11 opening and 10 closing reports 2016–2026: opens usually around June 12, as late as June 24; closes usually around November 29, as early as November 3. The Forest Service itself publishes only status plus a last-updated date and the note "Not maintained for winter travel, Snowmobile trail system" — these dated figures are crowdsourced, not a WMNF publication.
offroad.note: Highest elevation reached by a public road in New Hampshire, and one of the last WMNF roads to open each spring — an early-autumn stop is well inside the window, a spring one would not be. Many dispersed campsites, mostly on the north side toward Valley Road, 14-day max and you must occupy the first night. Mostly a car and a half wide.

offroad.name: Sandwich Notch Road
offroad.distance: 7.9 mi
offroad.difficulty: 1 (Easy) — the easiest of the local set; well-maintained forest road
offroad.season: Opens usually around May 12, as late as June 3; closes usually around October 28, from 14 opening and 8 closing reports 2013–2026. Note the late-October closing average — this is the one road in the set that can shut before the others. WMNF lists it as maintained by the town of Sandwich and NOT maintained for winter travel.
offroad.note: FR 98. Established 1801 and laid out as a route from the Pemigewasset valley to the seacoast; cellar holes still line it. Points of interest along the way: Upper and Lower Hall Ponds, Kiah Pond, Gillman Hall Cemetery and Beede Falls.

offroad.name: Tripoli Road
offroad.distance: 8.2 mi
offroad.difficulty: 1 (Easy) — very well maintained and mostly gravel; the hardest parts are the few stretches of unmaintained, badly deteriorated pavement
offroad.season: Opens usually around May 21, as late as May 31; closes usually around November 19, as early as November 1, from 12 opening and 10 closing reports 2015–2026.
offroad.note: FR 30. Built by the Forest Service in 1934 with CCC help and named for the Tripoli Mill; runs the pass between Mt Tecumseh and Mt Osceola. Popular for trailhead and campsite access. Bear and moose activity especially at night, and no cell service in the middle section.

offroad.name: Slippery Brook
offroad.distance: 4.6 mi. WMNF describes FR 17 and FR 38 together as a 7-mile road system commonly known as Town Hall Road.
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — gravel, well maintained in the summer months
offroad.season: Opens usually around May 24, as late as June 26; closes usually around November 29, as early as November 14, from 12 opening and 10 closing reports 2014–2026. Multiple gates close depending on snow levels and it is not maintained in winter.
offroad.note: This is National Forest System Road 17, in Jackson and Chatham. Camping and fire restrictions are in force 1 June 2026 to 1 June 2031: no camping within a quarter mile of the road except at designated sites marked with a tent symbol, and no wood or charcoal fires in the same band except at those sites — pressurised-fuel stoves are permitted. Worth knowing before planning a fire.

offroad.name: East Branch Saco River
offroad.distance: 3.3 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — dirt road, not plowed in winter, with one rough spot near the end by the beaver bog
offroad.season: Opens usually around May 26, as late as June 24; closes usually around November 24, as early as November 9, from 10 opening and 10 closing reports 2016–2026.
offroad.note: Resolved: this is East Branch Road, FR 38 — the East Branch of the Saco, in Jackson and Chatham, not the East Branch Pemigewasset — and it is the companion to Slippery Brook FR 17 in the Town Hall Road system. Well-maintained dirt and gravel hugging the river, with pull-offs for camping and trailheads and a bridge crossing; dead-ends at a hiking trail. The same quarter-mile camping and fire restrictions as FR 17 apply through 2031.

bar-harbor-me.dogs: ALLOWED on most trails — 100 miles of trail and 45 miles of carriage road, leash 6 ft. Acadia is one of the most dog-friendly national parks on this entire trip. Six trails are closed to pets outright: Precipice, BEEHIVE, Ladder Trail to Dorr Mountain, Beech Cliffs, Perpendicular (Mansell Mountain), and Jordan Cliffs between Penobscot East Trail and the carriage road. Nine more are "not recommended".
bar-harbor-me.dogs_note: The Beehive is named on this card AND is one of the six trails Acadia closes to dogs — the iron-rung climb. Everything else here is open to the dog, including Cadillac South Ridge and Gorham Mountain.
