offroad.name: Seal Cove Road
offroad.distance: NPS gives 2.17 miles, from the park boundary in Southwest Harbor to State Route 102; onX measures its own track at 2.7 mi, probably including connectors. Use the NPS figure.
offroad.difficulty: NPS publishes no scale; it described spring conditions as "Deep ruts, exposed culverts, and downed wood." onX rates it 2 (Easy).
offroad.season: Acadia's gravel roads close to motor vehicles around November 15 and reopen by May 15, weather and conditions permitting.
offroad.note: NPS opens this one first of the three west-side fire roads each spring, so it is the safest bet at the shoulders. Runs from Tremont Road at the west end to Main Street at the east, giving access to several trailheads plus Western Mountain Road. Recent reports call it washboarded with no significant views — the quiet is the point, not the scenery.

offroad.name: Western Mountain Road
offroad.distance: NPS: 3.32 miles including connecting unpaved roads (onX independently measures 3.3 mi)
offroad.difficulty: onX rates it 2 (Easy) — non-technical unless after heavy rain or in winter
offroad.season: Closes around November 15, reopens by May 15 weather permitting. NPS has published delayed spring openings for this road specifically after winter freeze-thaw damage, opening it only after Seal Cove Road.
offroad.note: NPS extent is from the park boundary west of the Worcester landfill to Seal Cove Pond. These are multi-purpose roads with walkers and cyclists as well as cars, so drive them accordingly. A loop from the Bald Mountain parking area via Western Mountain Road to Seal Cove Road runs roughly 3.2 miles. Gravel forestry surface with soft sand spots that turn to mud after heavy rain, and not always wide enough for two vehicles to pass.

offroad.name: Long Pond Fire Road
offroad.distance: 4.2 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — non-technical unless after heavy rain or during winter
offroad.season: NPS: on November 15, gravel roads in the park close to motor vehicle traffic, including Seal Cove Road, Western Mountain Roads and the Long Pond Fire Road. Reopened by May 15, weather and conditions permitting.
offroad.note: One of the few dirt roads in Acadia where you get away from the crowds. Starts at Tremont Road and reaches several trailheads plus a good swimming spot on Long Pond, Hodgdon Pond and Seal Cove Pond. Gravel forestry road with soft sand that turns muddy after rain; not always wide enough for two vehicles. Park entrance pass required. On the winter snowmobile question, the park's unplowed fire roads are generally open to snowmobiles, but no authority page names this road specifically — 36 CFR 7.56 designates the Long Pond TRUCK Road, which is a different road.

offroad.name: Donnell Pond
offroad.distance: 3.3 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — a gravel road with some rough washed-out areas, getting progressively rougher
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall. Maine Bureau of Parks and Lands publishes no gate dates but warns that many access roads are not plowed in winter unless timber harvesting is under way.
offroad.note: Mostly wide open, though some spur roads narrow considerably, and sections double as snowmobile trail in winter. Camping is allowed but campfires are prohibited outside established sites. A damaged bridge has turned people around partway, with the road continuing beyond it. The state authority for the unit is Maine BPL's Donnell Pond Public Reserved Land page, which names Black Mountain Road and Dynamite Brook Rd but publishes no road condition detail — Eastern Public Lands Office (207) 941-4412. Caveat: the listing's start point sits toward the Tunk Lake end, so which of the unit's gravel roads this actually is cannot be confirmed.

offroad.name: Narraguagus Lake
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — mostly gravel with a few muddy spots, easily driven in 2WD or 4WD
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall. No gate dates published, and probably none exist to find.
offroad.note: This is the start of a much larger northward system signed as Trail 501, reaching genuinely remote country and ending below a large group of wind turbines before continuing to South Spectacle Pond Road — so it is as long as you want it to be. Recent reports mention construction vehicles and heavy traffic near the turbines. Honest limit: no authority — Maine BPL, IF&W, land trust or town — confirms a road here by name, and it is most likely private timberland under permissive access, which is why no published gate dates exist.

offroad.name: Frye Mountain - High Ridge to Getchell
offroad.distance: 6.3 mi listed; just over 8 miles as driven, including a 3-mile out-and-back spur to a second cemetery
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — gravel roads, mostly wide enough for two vehicles to pass
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall. Maine IF&W closes WMA roads seasonally after the firearm deer season ends, to protect the road infrastructure — but publishes no calendar date for it, tying the closure to the end of the season instead. Do not assume a date; this one needs a call.
offroad.note: A west-to-east crossing of the Frye Mountain State Game Management Area, passing Carter Cemetery. A few sections at lower elevations can flood. The WMA is about 5,200 acres across Knox, Montville and Morrill in Waldo County; IF&W has no dedicated page for it, so the Lands Management Program page is the best official source available.

offroad.name: Bald Mountain Trail
offroad.distance: 1.3 mi
offroad.difficulty: 3 (Easy) — one vehicle wide and entirely uphill, with sections around 25-degree incline, washouts, loose rock, and ledges near the summit
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall; no gate dates published.
offroad.note: Location flag: this listing sits at 44.831, -68.482, in inland Hancock County — 50-odd miles northeast of Camden and much closer to the Bar Harbor/Ellsworth stop, so it may be filed under the wrong stop. It is genuinely a driving route, not a hiking listing. The Camden-area Bald Mountain is a Coastal Mountains Land Trust preserve on Barnestown Road whose published activities are hiking, birding and snowshoeing, with no evidence of a drivable summit road — so if the Camden mountain was meant, there is nothing to link. Summit is shared with a hiking trail; a few snowmobile side trails off it are not 4x4 friendly.

offroad.name: Quarry Road Trail
offroad.distance: 2.4 mi
offroad.difficulty: 3 (Easy) — two steep inclines and some rocky terrain
offroad.note: Three problems, any one of which is disqualifying. It is in Waterville — the trailhead is behind the Home Depot — roughly 45 miles inland from Camden, so it is on the wrong stop. It is reported Permanently Closed with an official closed sign, by three separate people between Oct 2024 and Aug 2025. And its access classes are single track, 50-inch and 60-inch only, with no full-width class, so it is an ATV/UTV trail the pickup does not fit. Recommend dropping it rather than linking it.

offroad.name: Country Road
offroad.distance: 1.8 mi
offroad.difficulty: 1 (Easy) — well-maintained gravel road
offroad.season: Not maintained in winter. October Mountain State Forest is open sunrise to one half-hour after sunset.
offroad.note: This is the main entrance road into October Mountain State Forest, the largest state forest in Massachusetts at 16,500 acres, and it gives access to several areas of the park with views over the wetlands to the west. Worth knowing the forest's other reputation: DCR states the OHV trails at October Mountain are challenging and only suitable for the intermediate to expert rider — that is a different trail set from this road.

offroad.name: Beartown Mountain Road
offroad.distance: 3.2 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — unmaintained, with mildly stepped sections where the gravel thins and plenty of holes and ruts that fill with runoff
offroad.season: DCR: Beartown State Forest OHV season is open May 1st to the last Sunday in November, weather permitting; park hours sunrise to sunset. A late-October visit is inside that window.
offroad.note: Begins at Route 102 at an unlocked gate and runs south into the park, with remnants of old pavement still showing before the gravel starts about 2 miles in. Crosses the Appalachian Trail 0.2 mi from the end and finishes in a residential dirt lot.

offroad.name: Mount Wilcox Road
offroad.distance: 4 mi listed; the full loop is 4.3 miles
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — two cars wide in places, soft shoulders, steeper climbs on loose gravel; unmaintained after snow
offroad.season: Same DCR Beartown window: OHV season May 1st to the last Sunday in November, weather permitting.
offroad.note: The main loop through Beartown State Forest, starting and ending off Benedict Pond Road and climbing from 1,600 to 2,100 ft. A short spur breaks off halfway to the summit, but the fire tower there is gated with no public access.

offroad.name: Ashley Lake Road
offroad.distance: 2.3 mi
offroad.difficulty: 3 (Easy) — a very bumpy road with occasional mud holes and small ledges that deepen in wet seasons
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall.
offroad.note: Currently obstructed, and this is the live problem: a report of 26 Jul 2026 describes a massive downed tree about 500 feet in from the south that ATVs and dirt bikes can pass but full-size vehicles cannot, and 2025 reports describe another tree plus heavy overgrowth that will stripe a full-size truck. Part of the route is a corduroy road — logs laid across the direction of travel — which is very rough. It runs through October Mountain State Forest past Ashley Lake, Sandwash Reservoir, Clapp Pond and Mud Pond, and the north end exits at a gate on Washington Mountain Road that has turned people around. No Pittsfield water-department access restriction could be sourced either way.

offroad.name: Greylock Road
offroad.distance: 2.9 mi
offroad.difficulty: 1 (Easy) — no harder than many dirt roads, but not frequently maintained, so fallen trees often block it
offroad.season: onX: open June through October only. For context, DCR's separate Mount Greylock Auto Roads ran May 16 to October 30 in 2026 — so a 27 October arrival clears both, but only by about three days and only weather permitting.
offroad.note: Resolved: this is a separate gravel road, NOT one of DCR's paved Notch/Rockwell/Summit auto roads — it is a quieter alternative ascent that eventually meets the paved main road and continues to the peak. Two status reports describe downed trees worth turning back for, so the gate date is not the only thing that can stop you. Note DCR's new rule that vehicles over 22 feet are prohibited on the Greylock Auto Roads and to the summit; the pickup is unaffected.

offroad.name: Del Reeves & North Mulford Roads
offroad.distance: 5 mi
offroad.difficulty: 1 (Easy) — nothing technical, a few bumps and the occasional mud hole after rain
offroad.season: Best time listed as spring, summer, fall AND winter — the only route in this set rated for all four, with a December snow run reported Open.
offroad.note: Forest correction that matters for planning: this is Meshomasic State Forest in Portland, not Naugatuck — roughly 35 to 45 miles east, across the Connecticut River, so it cannot be run from the same base as Cold Springs Road. Unmaintained, mostly dirt with some gravel. Numerous pull-offs, and one highlight is an old Nike missile site. The best-evidenced of the four, with status reports running through Aug 2026 and all reporting Open.

offroad.name: Del Reeves Road
offroad.distance: 3.2 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — a simple forest road, straightforward to navigate
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall. Graded state forest road, closed at sunset.
offroad.note: Also Meshomasic State Forest in Portland, not Naugatuck — same 35-to-45-mile eastward correction as the linked version above. Mostly dirt with a few gravel sections; doable in nearly any vehicle, but the ruts deepen and it turns muddy after rain. Several good pull-offs along it. Land owner of record is Connecticut DEEP.

offroad.name: Cold Springs Road
offroad.distance: 0.8 mi
offroad.difficulty: 2 (Easy) — unmaintained, weather-sensitive, mostly one vehicle wide with multiple deep ruts and small off-camber sections
offroad.season: Best summer and fall.
offroad.note: The only one of the four that really is in Naugatuck State Forest. Runs directly alongside an active railroad, and ends at the Spruce Brook Trail parking area. A minimum of 12 inches of ground clearance is recommended for the ruts and mud holes. Worth a call to CT DEEP Forestry first: the DEEP West Block map carries the notice that the roads and trails in that block are multi-use non-motorized except snowmobiles, and since this road ends at a West Block trailhead the likeliest reading is that it is an approach road with the non-motorized rule applying beyond the parking area — but DEEP does not say so, and none of these four road names appears on either Naugatuck map.

offroad.name: Filley Road
offroad.distance: 1.8 mi
offroad.difficulty: 1 (Easy) — very simple dirt and gravel; proper throttle control needed to avoid slipping in 2WD
offroad.season: Best spring, summer, fall and winter.
offroad.note: Third forest, third correction: this is Cockaponset State Forest, not Naugatuck. It serves as an entrance to the Cockaponset trail system and opens onto further trails in the forest — worth taking as a way in rather than as a destination in itself.

Delaware Water Gap National Recreation A.entity: Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area

offroad.name: Big Pocono State Park summit road
offroad.season: Park closed early December, reopens the first week of April; sunrise to sunset when open
offroad.note: DCNR warns of steep grades and says not to attempt the drive with a trailer in tow. It also states municipal road maintenance is not provided on the access roadway and that seasonal closures of it will occur, so the April reopening is a target rather than a promise. DCNR publishes no length for the summit loop; the 1.4-mile figure that circulates is not on the official page and is not recorded here.

offroad.name: Old Mine Road, NJ side north of Millbrook Village
offroad.note: NPS treats this as a windshield tour of a roughly 250-year-old route and notes the original unpaved roadbed survives on foot at spots such as the Van Campen Inn and Hamilton Ridge near Millbrook. The park publishes no mileage, no surface breakdown and no seasonal closure for the drive itself; the page directs road-condition questions to the park at the number it lists.

offroad.name: Caledonia to Pine Grove Furnace forest roads
offroad.note: DCNR's Michaux map index carries the two documents that actually answer which of these roads can be driven: the Michaux State Forest Public Use Map and a self-guided 'Auto Tour of Michaux State Forest', both PDFs. The index itself publishes no mileage for the auto tour, and the PDFs were not read here. The separate ATV trail map on the same page is a different system and is not the drivable road network.

offroad.name: Michaux State Forest gravel road network, South Mountain
offroad.note: DCNR's forest page confirms the authority and links a Michaux State Forest Recreation Guide PDF, but publishes nothing about which roads are open, gated or seasonally closed. Pennsylvania does not run an MVUM system like the national forests, so the Public Use Map on the maps page is the only thing that distinguishes drivable forest roads from gated administrative ones.

staunton-va.dogs: ALLOWED on most trails — Shenandoah is one of the few national parks that permits dogs on trails, with fewer than 20 of 500+ trail miles off-limits. Leash 6 ft, physical leash. Prohibited: Fox Hollow, STONY MAN (blue-blazed portion to the summit), Limberlost, the Old Rag trails, Post Office Junction to Old Rag Shelter, Dark Hollow Falls, Story of the Forest, Bearfence Mountain and Frazier Discovery.
staunton-va.dogs_note: Two of this stop's trails are on Shenandoah's short prohibited list — Stony Man's blue-blazed summit portion and the Old Rag trails (Ridge Access, Ridge, Saddle). Everything ELSE in the park is open to the dog, which still makes this one of the best stops on the trip for walking together; it is just that both trails currently named here happen to be exceptions. Worth adding dog-legal Shenandoah trails to this card.

offroad.name: George Washington NF gravel roads, North River / Todd Lake district
offroad.season: Todd Lake Recreation Area open mid-May to late October
offroad.note: Forest Service directions run 1.1 miles on SR 718 (Stokesville Road) to the FR 95 / FR 101 junction, then 3.1 miles on FR 95 (North River Road) to Todd Lake. The page does not state whether FR 95 is gravel or paved and publishes no vehicle restriction. FR 95 is also the lower end of the North River Trail, which climbs to FR 85 (Shenandoah Mountain Road) — the same road as the Reddish Knob route below, so the two can be linked.

offroad.name: Reddish Knob road (FR 85 from Briery Branch, west of Harrisonburg)
offroad.difficulty: onX rating 2 (Easy) — "easy dirt and gravel trail with just a few rutted and rocky spots"
offroad.season: onX lists spring, summer, fall and winter
offroad.note: onX rates this for high-clearance, full-width vehicles and puts the observation point at 4,397 ft. The adjoining Flagpole Knob route meets it at Briery Branch Gap and has its own onX listing at 12.8 miles, also difficulty 2 — the pair make one long day if the weather holds. Note the two are not equivalent: Flagpole's FR 85 approach is reported as much rougher than the Reddish Knob asphalt spur.

lexington-va.authority: National Park Service — Shenandoah / Blue Ridge Parkway
lexington-va.dogs: ALLOWED on most trails — Shenandoah is one of the few national parks that permits dogs on trails, with fewer than 20 of 500+ trail miles off-limits. Leash 6 ft, physical leash. Prohibited: Fox Hollow, STONY MAN (blue-blazed portion to the summit), Limberlost, the Old Rag trails, Post Office Junction to Old Rag Shelter, Dark Hollow Falls, Story of the Forest, Bearfence Mountain and Frazier Discovery.

offroad.name: George Washington & Jefferson NF gravel roads, North Mountain west of Lexington
offroad.note: Unlisted. No Forest Service page and no off-road database covers this road network as a named route. The forest's Motor Vehicle Use Map is the only authority on which of these roads are open and to which vehicle class, and GWJNF publishes one forest-wide MVUM rather than per-district ones — so plan from the MVUM, not from a route listing.

offroad.name: George Washington National Forest roads (near Natural Bridge, off Rt. 812)
offroad.note: Unlisted, same situation as North Mountain: the Forest Service publishes district topographic maps and a single forest-wide MVUM, but no page for this road network and no named route in any off-road database. The MVUM carries the vehicle-class and seasonal designations for each road.

offroad.name: James River Face Wilderness access roads (Belfast Trail / Petites Gap)
offroad.season: Forest Service lists the trail open year round
offroad.note: Forest Service directions take the left fork onto VA 781 (Petites Gap Road) and run about 1.0 mile to the parking area. The page grades the Belfast Trail itself Moderate to Difficult over 2.3 miles — that is the walk to the Devil's Marbleyard boulder field, not the drive. The Forest Service says nothing about the road's surface or its FS 35 designation, so no surface claim is recorded.

offroad.name: Cunard river access road
offroad.season: Closed every November through March, from the Brooklyn Mine Trail parking lot down to the river; open April to October. NPS says this pattern continues through 2027.
offroad.note: This is the annual winter closure for road and drainage work, not weather. When open, NPS reports the lower sections are gravel and there are one-lane stretches that cause delays. The closure takes out vehicle, bike and pedestrian access to the Cunard river access, the angler's access and Brooklyn campground together. The park's closures page was last updated 6 Aug 2026 — check it again before the stop.

offroad.name: Fayette Station Road (CR 82)
offroad.distance: 8 mi
offroad.season: No seasonal closure published
offroad.note: One-way, and the binding restriction is height not length: NPS states vehicles over 12 ft tall cannot complete the route because of the clearance under a railroad bridge, and does not recommend large vehicles, RVs or trailers on the hairpins. Allow 30–45 minutes without stops. The road passes under the New River Gorge Bridge three times.

offroad.name: Keeneys Creek Road down to Nuttallburg
offroad.distance: about 4 mi — NPS gives ~3.5 mi to the wayside exhibit and 0.5 mi more to the Nuttallburg parking area
offroad.note: NPS calls it narrow, winding and steep, part paved and part gravel, with much of it single lane so drivers have to pull off to let others by. Trailers, RVs and motorhomes are specifically advised against — limited parking and difficult to turn around at the bottom. Separate from the road, the Keeney's Creek Rail Trail is closed above the Conveyor Trail junction for flood damage.

offroad.name: WV 25 to Thurmond
offroad.distance: 7 mi from the Glen Jean exit off US 19
offroad.note: The NPS directions page gives the seven miles but publishes no surface or vehicle guidance for WV 25 — the 'narrow, winding, not recommended for RVs or trailers' description that circulates is not on an NPS page that could be opened here, so it is not recorded as fact. Worth knowing separately: the Rend Trail, which starts at Thurmond, is closed from both trailheads until roughly December 2027 per the park's road and trail closures page.

offroad.name: Brown Mountain OHV Trail System, Pisgah NF
offroad.distance: 34 mi of designated trails
offroad.season: Closed 1 January to the first weekend in April, along with Curtis Creek Campground, on the Grandfather Ranger District seasonal closure list (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/northcarolina/about-area/faqs/seasonal-closures)
offroad.note: This is a ticketed OHV trail system, not a forest-road drive — passes go through Recreation.gov. Before counting on it: the Forest Service page defines the ATV class here as under 60 inches wide and does not state anywhere that full-size 4WD trucks may use the system. The commonly repeated claim that Jeeps and 4WDs are limited to Trail 8 and part of Trail 1 is not on any Forest Service page that could be opened, so it is unverified. Call the Grandfather Ranger District before driving out.

offroad.name: Pisgah NF gravel roads around Edgemont and Mortimer
offroad.season: Mortimer Campground open 31 March to 31 October; the Grandfather Ranger District closure list gates the Mortimer area 1 November to the first weekend in April
offroad.note: The Forest Service confirms the campground and its position in the Wilson Creek Wild & Scenic corridor south of Grandfather Mountain, but publishes no road numbers, mileage or surface for the Edgemont loop. Neither Roseboro Road (FSR 981) nor Edgemont-Pinola Road (FSR 464) has a Forest Service page, so their condition is unsourced. Note this stop's route and the Wilson Creek entry below share the same road corridor from opposite ends.

offroad.name: Wilson Creek Gorge / Brown Mountain Beach Road, Pisgah NF
offroad.distance: not published on the free listing
offroad.difficulty: not published on the free listing
offroad.note: Trails Offroad classes it a Scout Route and shows 4/5 from 3 reviews; distance, difficulty and waypoints are behind the paywall. The listing places it in Adako, Caldwell County, running through the Wilson Creek Gorge past the Mortimer ghost town. The Forest Service's Wilson Creek Wild and Scenic River Area page confirms the area is open all year but says nothing at all about the road.

offroad.name: Bent Creek gravel road network, from camp
offroad.note: Worth checking before planning a drive here. The Forest Service research station — this is an experimental forest, roughly 6,000 acres, the oldest federal one east of the Mississippi — permits hiking, biking and horseback riding on designated trails, and describes the gravel roads themselves as open to bicycles, horses and hikers. It nowhere says the road network is open to private motor vehicles, and it asks that research study sites not be disturbed. Treat this as a bike-and-walk network from camp unless the Pisgah Ranger District says otherwise.

offroad.name: Curtis Creek Road (FR 482), Old Fort
offroad.season: Closed 1 January to the first weekend in April (Grandfather Ranger District), together with Curtis Creek Campground
offroad.note: The Forest Service closure list writes this road as FR 428, not FR 482 as the card has it. One of the two numbers is wrong and it is worth settling with the Grandfather Ranger District rather than discovering it at a junction. No Forest Service page publishes the road's length or surface. Separately, this whole district was closed after Hurricane Helene and has been reopening in stages, so confirm current status close to the date.

offroad.name: FR 475 past the Davidson River fish hatchery toward Gloucester Gap
offroad.note: The forest's live Helene status page is the right authority here, but FS 475 is not named on it — only Yellow Gap Road is. Forest Service news coverage that could not be opened directly reports FS 475 open from US 276 to Cove Creek Group Campground and closed from there to the Daniel Ridge trailhead for a bridge replacement; that is not recorded as fact. This road is the one that reaches Gloucester Gap at the FS 471 junction, so a closed middle section breaks the through route. Call the Pisgah Ranger District.

offroad.name: Yellow Gap Road (FR 1206), Pisgah Ranger District
offroad.note: Currently not a through route. The Forest Service Helene status page has FR 1206 open from US 276 near the Cradle of Forestry as far as Wolf Ford Horse Camp, and closed from Wolf Ford Horse Camp to North Mills River Campground — so it is an out-and-back from the 276 end, not the Brevard-to-Mills River link. No length is published by the Forest Service.

bryson-city-nc.authority: National Park Service — Great Smoky Mountains
bryson-city-nc.dogs: PROHIBITED on trails, with exactly two exceptions: the Gatlinburg Trail and the Oconaluftee River Trail. Leash 6 ft on those. NPS actively discourages bringing pets because most trails are off-limits.
bryson-city-nc.dogs_exception: Gatlinburg Trail and Oconaluftee River Trail only.
bryson-city-nc.dogs_note: Oconaluftee is the accessible one from this side — the Bryson City stop already names the Oconaluftee Visitor Center in its highlights, so the dog-legal walk is the one you were going to anyway.

offroad.name: Cove Creek Road / Old NC 284 into Cataloochee
offroad.season: The park's seasonal road schedule lists Cataloochee Road as open year round, two-lane gravel, subject to weather closures. Old NC 284 has no fixed dates — the park closes it in severe weather or heavy rain.
offroad.note: NPS describes Cove Creek as a winding gravel road with steep drop-offs and no guardrails, narrow enough that drivers may have to stop or back up to pass. Old NC 284, the back way in from Big Creek, is also winding gravel. Post-Helene the Cataloochee entrance road was open to vehicles only as far as Beech Grove School with the upper section closed — from the park's reopening release, https://www.nps.gov/grsm/learn/news/great-smoky-mountains-national-park-to-reopen-portions-of-cataloochee-on-april-4.htm. Confirm before the drive.

offroad.name: Heintooga Ridge Road / Heintooga Round Bottom Road
offroad.season: Heintooga Ridge Road 15 May – 31 Oct. Heintooga Round Bottom Road: opening date TBD, as is Straight Fork Road, both still recovering from Hurricane Helene.
offroad.note: Two different roads under one name and only the first half is confirmed. Heintooga Ridge Road is paved and two-way, and motorhomes, buses and vans longer than 25 ft are prohibited — the towed pickup is fine. The Round Bottom (Balsam Mountain) half, the one-way gravel descent toward Cherokee that makes this a through route rather than a dead end, had no published opening date when checked. Do not plan the loop until the park posts a date.

offroad.name: Parson Branch Road
offroad.distance: 8 mi
offroad.season: 1 May – 9 Nov
offroad.note: One-way gravel leaving Cades Cove — you exit at US 129 and cannot come back the way you came. NPS recommends high clearance and restricts large vehicles. It reopened in 2022 after a six-year closure for hazard trees, and the park still closes it for high water, so it is the least dependable of the four here.

offroad.name: Rich Mountain Road
offroad.season: 10 Apr – 9 Nov
offroad.note: One-way out of Cades Cove toward Townsend, with the park's standard restriction on these roads — no motorhomes, buses, or vans longer than 25 ft, and no passenger vehicles towing trailers. The schedule publishes no length. Same one-way trap as Parson Branch: it is a way out of the cove, not a there-and-back.

offroad.name: Cherokee National Forest gravel roads above the Ocoee (US 64 corridor)
offroad.note: The authority is the 2024 Ocoee Ranger District Motor Vehicle Use Map (https://www.fs.usda.gov/media/233244) plus a companion sheet of seasonal and special vehicle designations (https://www.fs.usda.gov/media/233242) — both linked from this page and both confirmed to resolve. They are scanned PDFs and could not be read as text here, so the actual gate dates are not transcribed; the seasonal sheet is the one to open on a phone before driving. Paper copies are free at the Forest Service offices in Benton and Cleveland.

offroad.name: Prentice Cooper State Forest road network, above the Tennessee River Gorge
offroad.season: Tower Drive past Pot Point Gate closed 20 Dec – 15 Mar. Tower Drive south of Pot Point Road, plus Elder Point, Long Point and Inman Point, closed to motorized use from late April to early July for turkey nesting.
offroad.note: Two things beyond the gates. Motorized vehicles must stay on designated roads and the forest speed limit is 25 mph. And during managed hunts everything west of SR 27 (Suck Creek Road) is closed to all visitors except licensed hunters — the hunt dates are set by TWRA each year and are the thing most likely to shut this stop's day out, so check the WMA calendar rather than assuming the gate dates cover it.

offroad.name: Ouachita National Forest gravel roads, Lake Ouachita north shore
offroad.note: The managing authority for the whole north shore — about 406,000 acres. The page names a Winona Scenic Drive but publishes no mileage, road numbers or surface for it, and no individual road pages exist. One live alert on the page has Henderson Hill Road (FSR 689) partially closed. Which roads are open, and to what vehicle class, lives only on the forest's MVUM.

trails.name: Cedar Falls Trail
trails.was: Rock House Cave / Bear Cave Trail — a different trail
trails.note_source: Arkansas' most photographed place: from Mather Lodge steeply down Cedar Creek Canyon to the 95 ft falls. No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name kept; no constructed slug.

trails.name: Signal Hill Trail
trails.was: Bear Hollow Trail — a different trail
trails.note_source: To the highest point in Arkansas at 2,753 ft. No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name kept; no constructed slug.

offroad.name: Ozark National Forest gravel forest roads (Cove Lake / Magazine vicinity)
offroad.note: Unlisted. The Mt. Magazine Ranger District is the managing authority and its office page confirms the district, but the Forest Service publishes no page for Cove Lake or for the district's forest-road network, and no off-road database carries a named route here. The district's only current road alert is Morgan Mtn Rd, partially closed for road repair. Plan from the Ozark-St. Francis MVUM.

offroad.name: Ozark National Forest roads on the north flank of Magazine
offroad.note: Unlisted, same as the Cove Lake network above — the district page is the only authority that confirms these roads are Forest Service, and nothing publishes their numbers, surface or gate dates. Note this stop carries two offroad entries for what may be the same road network; worth folding into one with `same_as` if the tags agree.

trails.name: Whitaker Point Trail (Hawksbill Crag)
trails.was: Buffalo River Trail (Ponca to Steel Creek) — a different trail; Hawksbill Crag is the marquee walk here
trails.note_source: The narrow sandstone overhang 200 ft above the valley — the most photographed spot in the Ozarks.

trails.name: Lost Valley Trail
trails.note_source: Along Clark Creek past natural bridges to Eden Falls and Cobb Cave. Crushed rock to natural surface. No direct listing url surfaced in search. Name kept; no constructed slug.

offroad.name: AR-43/74 Ponca-Boxley Valley Loop (truck-only)
offroad.note: These are paved state highways, not forest roads — NPS routes visitors to the Jasper/Ponca upper district via Highway 7 or Highway 43 south from Harrison. The park publishes no loop mileage. One genuine warning from the park: GPS is unreliable in this area and has sent numerous visitors the wrong way onto dirt roads, which matters more here than the pavement does.

offroad.name: Cave Mountain / Fallsville forest roads
offroad.note: Unlisted. Neither the National Park Service nor the Forest Service publishes a page naming these roads, and no off-road database carries them as a route. The nearest sourced statement is the park's blanket warning that access roads in this area may be unpaved, in some cases extremely rocky, and may require four-wheel drive and/or high clearance. Fallsville sits on the Ozark NF Big Piney district, so its MVUM is the authority for that half.

offroad.name: Cave Mountain Road (to Hawksbill Crag trailhead)
offroad.note: Unlisted, and this is the weakest-sourced route in this batch. It is a Newton County road running to the Upper Buffalo Wilderness trailhead, so it belongs to neither the park nor the Forest Service, and neither publishes anything on it. Every description of it as rough, rocky and steep, and every 'about four miles to the parking area' figure, is user-generated. The park's general warning about unpaved, extremely rocky access roads needing 4WD or high clearance is the only sourced statement that applies.

offroad.name: Erbie Road
offroad.note: The park has no page for Erbie Road itself; what it does publish is the general rule that access roads here may be unpaved, in some cases extremely rocky, and may require four-wheel drive and/or high clearance. An Erbie campground map PDF exists and resolves at https://www.nps.gov/buff/planyourvisit/upload/Erbie-Campground-Map-Final-Edit-2017.pdf (confirmed 200; contents not readable as text here) and would be the thing to open on a phone.

offroad.name: Kyles Landing entrance road
offroad.note: Same position as Erbie — the only sourced statement is the park's warning that access roads may be unpaved, extremely rocky and may require 4WD and/or high clearance. The widely repeated figures of roughly 2.8 to 3 miles of steep gravel off AR 74 are not on any NPS page that could be opened, so they are not recorded. Both Kyles Landing campground map URLs that surfaced return 404, so there is no PDF to fall back on.

offroad.name: Push Mountain Road & Sylamore Ranger District forest roads
offroad.season: Alert opened 7 April 2025 after the 2025 storms and stands until further notice
offroad.note: Push Mountain Road itself is a state highway, not a forest road, and the Forest Service publishes nothing on it. What this alert does settle is the district's gravel network after the 2025 floods and tornado: Cole Fork Road is still closed, and the Syllamo mountain-bike system including the Jack's Branch and Bad Branch loops and its trailhead is still closed for tornado damage. Barkshed, Gunner Pool and Blanchard Springs campgrounds and day-use area have all reopened.

offroad.name: Sylamore District forest roads to Gunner Pool and Barkshed
offroad.season: Both sites open all year; water at Gunner Pool is seasonal, April to November
offroad.note: The Forest Service gives the road numbers for both. Gunner Pool is FSR 1102, gravel, and the Forest Service calls the approach a steep, winding dirt road not recommended for large recreation vehicles. Barkshed is AR 14 west from Mountain View 17.3 miles, then FSR 1115 (gravel) 2.1 miles, then FSR 1112 1.4 miles — https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/ozark-stfrancis/recreation/barkshed-recreation-area — also not recommended for large trailers or RVs. Both reopened after the 2025 storms.

offroad.name: Shores Lake / Salt Fork forest roads
offroad.distance: about 10 mi of FSR 1501 under reconstruction
offroad.season: Work began autumn 2025, expected to finish summer 2027; the Forest Service expects the road to stay open to traffic through most of it
offroad.note: FSR 1501 runs from AR 23 on the east to AR 215 on the west near Shores Lake — culverts, reshaping, fresh gravel and overlook parking. Hurricane Road (FSR 1003) work is already complete. This lands squarely in the trip's window, so expect active construction rather than a closure. No Forest Service page names a 'Salt Fork' road, so that half of the entry is unsourced.

offroad.name: White Rock Mountain Road
offroad.distance: FSR 1505 for 8 mi (first 0.5 mi paved, then gravel), then FSR 1003 west for 2.5 mi of gravel, from AR 215 north of Mulberry
offroad.season: Recreation area open all year
offroad.note: Part of FSR 1003 is still out. Per the Forest Service alert last updated 22 May 2026 (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/ozark-stfrancis/alerts/fsr-1003-white-rock-road-closure-partially-lifted), the stretch between Bliss Ridge Road (FSR 1505-1) and Wood's Gap is repaired and open, but the eastern slide near Spirits Creek Bridge remains closed with no estimate of when or if it will be repaired. Approach from the west via Hurricane Road or from the north via Boles Gap Road (FSR 1505-2). Summit is 2,289 ft with CCC stone cabins and lodge.

offroad.name: White Rock Mountain Road (Ozark National Forest)
offroad.distance: FSR 1505 for 8 mi (first 0.5 mi paved, then gravel), then FSR 1003 west for 2.5 mi of gravel, from AR 215 north of Mulberry
offroad.season: Recreation area open all year
offroad.note: Duplicate — this is the same road as the 'White Rock Mountain Road' entry on this stop, listed twice under two names. Worth folding into one with `same_as` rather than shipping both. Same caveat applies: FSR 1003's eastern slide near Spirits Creek Bridge is still closed with no repair estimate, so come in from the west or the north.

offroad.name: Caney Creek Wilderness access roads (Shady Lake / Forest Service network)
offroad.note: Unlisted. The Mena-Oden Ranger District is the managing authority and its office page confirms it, but the Forest Service publishes no page for Shady Lake, for Caney Creek Wilderness access, or for the surrounding road network, and no off-road database lists a named route. The Ouachita MVUM is the only authority on which of these roads are open and to what vehicle class.

offroad.name: Cossatot Falls access road
offroad.note: Arkansas State Parks is the managing authority and its park page is the right link, but it publishes nothing about the access road — no surface, no mileage, no clearance requirement and no flood closure policy, despite the falls area being the part of the park most likely to be cut off by high water. Everything about the road's condition is currently unsourced; the park visitor centre is the place to settle it.

offroad.name: Ouachita National Forest roads (FR 106, FR 25 and others)
offroad.note: Unlisted. Neither FR 106 nor FR 25 has a Forest Service page on the Mena-Oden district, and no off-road database lists them. Be careful with the numbers: FR 106 is also a road number on the Grandfather district in North Carolina (Dobson Knob), so a search on the bare number returns the wrong state. The Ouachita MVUM is the authority.

offroad.name: Rich Mountain fire-tower spur
offroad.distance: the byway itself is 54 mi
offroad.season: Byway open year round
offroad.note: The Forest Service page covers the byway that runs the spine of Rich Mountain and Winding Stair Mountain, but says nothing about a fire tower or about any spur road off it — so the spur itself is effectively unlisted and only the parent byway is sourced. The byway is paved; whatever spur the card means is not described anywhere the Forest Service publishes.

offroad.name: Wolf Pen Gap OHV Trail System
offroad.note: A permitted OHV trail system on the Mena-Oden district, not a forest-road drive. The Forest Service lists Mena-Oden among its OHV districts but publishes no mileage, fee, permitted vehicle class or season for Wolf Pen Gap specifically. The same page carries a notice dated 1 June 2026 that USDA and the Forest Service are reviewing OHV policy, so the permit rules may not be what they are now by the time of the stop — confirm with the district before buying anything.

offroad.name: Movie Road (Alabama Hills)
offroad.distance: about 6 miles of graded gravel looping off US-395 through the rock formations and back
offroad.difficulty: not published as a grade. Graded dirt, no low range needed in dry conditions; the spurs off it get rougher
offroad.season: NO CONFLICT. Open year-round at about 4,500 ft. The stop arrives 27 Dec 2027 — snow is uncommon this low, but a winter storm turns the graded dirt greasy and the spurs soft, so pick the day.
offroad.note: Renamed from a vague plural to the one named route. BLM restricts vehicle and mountain-bike use to existing roads and trails — no cross-country driving in the Scenic Area, and the boulder fields are exactly where people are tempted. A free permit is needed to camp, not to drive; get it online, at the Eastern Sierra Interagency Visitor Center on US-395, or at the kiosks on Movie Road itself. BLM publishes a downloadable Movie Road brochure identifying the film locations, which is the point of the drive.

scenicDrives_patch.name: Movie Road, Alabama Hills
scenicDrives_patch.note: From the centre of Lone Pine, 2.7 mi west on Whitney Portal Road, then right onto Movie Road where the pavement ends. Graded gravel, about 6 mi through the rock maze past the western film locations before rejoining US-395; sources also describe a fuller 12 mi loop. BLM publishes a downloadable Movie Road brochure identifying the film sites. Congress designated the Alabama Hills a National Scenic Area in March 2019. Camping at designated sites needs the free Alabama Hills permit.
scenicDrives_patch.season: No gate; usable year-round. Arrive 27 Dec 2027 — cold, low sun, which is the good light here. Graded gravel can wash after storms.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: BLM Alabama Hills pages; BLM Alabama Hills National Scenic Area program page

other_links.label: BLM — Alabama Hills National Scenic Area

scenicDrives_patch.name: US-395 north through the Owens Valley
scenicDrives_patch.was_name: US-395 north toward the Owens Valley
scenicDrives_patch.note: The run up the middle of the Owens Valley with the Sierra crest on the left and the Inyo and White Mountains on the right. Caltrans has officially designated US-395 a state scenic highway from Fort Independence to Fort Springs Road in Inyo County, and again from the Inyo–Mono county line to south of Walker — the whole 200 mi is not uniformly designated. No single official byway page exists, so the Bishop visitor bureau's scenic-drives itinerary is the best available link.
scenicDrives_patch.season: Open year-round as a primary route. Arrive 27 Dec 2027 — winter storms bring chain controls and closures on 395; check Caltrans before a long day north.
scenicDrives_patch.note_source: Caltrans scenic-highway designation as reported on Wikipedia's US Route 395 in California; bishopvisitor.com

not_a_trail.problem: A graded gravel ROAD, not a trail — and a duplicate of the scenicDrives entry 'Movie Road, Alabama Hills' on this same stop. AllTrails does index it as 'Movie Road Trail' (251 reviews), but LINKS_STRATEGY §3 rejects roads from the trails box and §6 says to deduplicate across boxes before adding. Drop it here; the drive already carries the BLM link.

lone-pine.dogs: BLM Bishop Field Office publishes no pet rule for the Alabama Hills at all — not on the scenic-area page, not on the Mobius Arch trail page, not in the 2022 brochure or the map and guide — so this is unknown, not permitted.

not_a_route.entry: The coach is appropriate for the main Alaska Highway.
not_a_route.problem: A statement about the coach on a paved highway. Not an offroad route by any reading — it belongs in the leg notes, if anywhere.

dawson-creek.dogs: On leash in every City of Dawson Creek park (Animal Responsibility Bylaw 4420 — Barbaree Park is the only off-leash area), which covers Chamberlain Nature Park and Leoppky Park; Radar Lake, the Rim Rocks wind-park paths and McQueen Slough are all outside the city and none of their managers publishes a dog rule.
dawson-creek.dogs_source_quote: No owner will permit the owner's animal to be at large in the City.

offroad.name: McCarthy Road
offroad.was_name: Drive the McCarthy Road to McCarthy & Kennecott (in the towed 4x4, not the motorhome)
offroad.distance: 59.4 miles one way, Chitina State Wayside to the McCarthy footbridge over the Kennicott River
offroad.difficulty: not graded by NPS. Usually driveable in 2WD, but soft shoulders, limited visibility and poor surface mean it is a slow, attentive drive rather than an easy one
offroad.season: Best late June through early September, when the road is clear of ice and snow. The stop arrives 15 Aug 2027 — squarely inside the good window, no conflict.
offroad.note: Pack-dirt and gravel on an old railbed. The state has spent heavily on it in recent years and it is well maintained in summer, but potholes and washboard hold you to 35 mph or below. NPS suggests two hours; allow three each way, and remember there is no vehicle bridge at the far end — you park at the Kennicott River and walk the footbridge into McCarthy. This is the entry the box was really about; the rig advice in the old name is now settled policy and has moved to the note.

offroad.name: O'Brien Creek Road
offroad.distance: about 3 miles from Chitina to the O'Brien Creek parking area — and that is where driveable road ends
offroad.difficulty: not a technical route. The short spur is ordinary rough gravel
offroad.season: The road is there year-round, but its whole character depends on the Copper River personal-use dipnet fishery, which runs periodically between about 7 June and 30 September. The stop arrives 15 Aug 2027, inside that window — expect the parking area busy with dipnetters and charter operators.
offroad.note: Worth correcting an expectation: this is not a 4x4 route, it is a three-mile spur. Beyond O'Brien Creek the old roadbed through Wood Canyon is extremely rough and undriveable — the bridge over the creek takes ATVs only, and the trail past it is an ATV route and a dangerous one. The DOT road project beyond O'Brien Creek has stalled. Also worth knowing before going: the local tribe has petitioned to close the road, which overlies a burial ground, so treat the area as sensitive.

not_a_route.problem: Duplicate — the same road is listed twice in this box, once as a verb phrase and once as 'O'Brien Creek Road (4x4)'. Folded into a single entry.

not_a_route.entry: Stop at the Wrangell-St. Elias NPS ranger station in Chitina
not_a_route.problem: A building, and a good idea, but not a route. Belongs in activities or points of interest. It is also where you would ask about McCarthy Road conditions, so it is worth keeping somewhere on the card.

offroad.name: Sage Creek Rim Road
offroad.difficulty: NPS: "a dirt/gravel road" that "can be rough during or after storms"
offroad.season: NPS: "may be temporarily closed during or after heavy rain or snow" and "may be closed in the winter due to weather conditions"
offroad.note: NPS allows 1–2 hours to drive it and publishes no mileage. It connects SD 44 near Scenic with the Badlands Loop Road (SD 240) north of Pinnacles Overlook, so it can be run as a leg rather than an out-and-back. Along it: Hay Butte and Badlands Wilderness overlooks, Roberts Prairie Dog Town, Sage Creek Basin and Sage Creek Campground. Road status by phone: 605-433-5361.

offroad.name: Sage Creek Rim Road (SD-590)
offroad.difficulty: NPS: "a dirt/gravel road" that "can be rough during or after storms"
offroad.season: NPS: "may be temporarily closed during or after heavy rain or snow" and "may be closed in the winter due to weather conditions"
offroad.note: Same road as the entry above — one route, listed twice in this box. NPS confirms the SD 590 designation and gives no mileage. Phone 605-433-5361 for status.

_dogs_verdict: Per stop: 'allowed' | 'prohibited' | 'partial' | absent. Absent means NOT RESEARCHED and renders no icon at all — a missing dog rule must never look like a green light. 'partial' means the authority names some trails and not others, so the verdict lives on the trail, not the stop.
_activities: Per-stop overrides for the highlights list. Each entry maps an activity's name to a verified entity: its real Wikipedia article, its direct AllTrails listing where it IS a trail, and the official page. Activities with an entry render real links and pills; activities without one keep the generic name-derived search links, which is the honest fallback until they are researched. `drop: true` removes a duplicate restatement of another activity.
_url_provenance: EVERY url here must be COPIED from a search result that returned it. Never construct a slug from a trail's name — alltrails slugs are unpredictable (--2, --3 suffixes, reworded titles) and a fabricated one looks exactly like a real one until it 404s in front of you at a trailhead. This rule exists because four urls were built from names in this file; three happened to be right and one was not, which is luck, not verification.
_auto: Entries marked auto:true were resolved by resolve_highlights.py — the headline reduced to candidate entity names and checked against Wikipedia's real article index. Exact hits only; a fuzzy match is treated as no match. Hand-written entries are richer and are never overwritten.
_search_note: Searching with allowed_domains=alltrails.com returns FEWER alltrails results than an open web search does. Warner Point, Horse Gulch and Piedra River were all recorded as 'no listing found' from a restricted search and all three have listings — found by searching the open web instead. Search open, then take the alltrails url from the results.
